title: First full census of Ethereum and Tezos works
body: Every file of every edition — 35,008 works, 106,392 files — was fetched through the public gateways wallets and browsers use. 17,563 works have all media content-addressed and resolving on ipfs.io. 184 works have content-addressed media that currently fails on a public gateway. 17,255 works' media was reachable only from our CDN, and 6 works depended on a third-party platform (figures corrected 2026-08-05 from the first published 17,261); they join the Bitmark-era works on the remediation path. These checks measure the artwork files; the metadata link and rendering are not yet measured.

title: Works that depend entirely on us, enumerated
body: Published the complete list of works whose only copy sits behind Feral File's own servers: 4,959 works across 215 series in 17 exhibitions, all minted on the Bitmark blockchain before Feral File moved to Ethereum and Tezos. Every series' media was checked and currently resolves. Remediation — a content-addressed copy for every work, so each resolves independently of us — is targeted within 2 to 3 months. The full census of Ethereum and Tezos works is running and publishes here when it completes.

title: Every Bitmark-era series now has a verified content-addressed copy
body: All 215 series — 398 GB, every file of every work whose only copy lived on our CDN — have been added to IPFS and verified byte-for-byte against the originals. The addresses are published in the pin manifest beside this page, so any collector, museum, or archive can hold a copy of any work with one command. The works' own references still point at our CDN; linking them to these copies is the next step.

title: The Feral File Archive is anchored on Ethereum
body: The Archive's manifest — every archival copy's address, for all 215 Bitmark-era series, a2p (the 2019-2020 artist-to-artist exchange Feral File grew out of; 144 works across two generations), and the Bitmark blockchain itself — is now recorded on Ethereum in the FeralFileArchiveRegistry at 0x9aF574cafe2C14161DEC1eAC11F7F2c281fCa34e, owned by Feral File's 2-of-3 custody Safe. For the archived collections, the registry on Ethereum points to their IPFS manifest with no Feral File server in the path; the works' own token references do not yet point at these copies — that reference phase is open. The registry keeps its full version history in contract storage, following the pattern set when the Bitmark blockchain was retired: root on Ethereum, data on IPFS.

title: Tightened this page's own claims to what the probes measure
body: Two external audits of this page found summary lines claiming more than the checks prove: the machine-readable mirrors said the site reports "whether each link answers" when it measures the artwork-media layer only. Every summary surface (page, Markdown, llms.txt, RSS, status.json) now states the same boundary: artwork media is measured, the metadata link and rendering are not yet. The probe date now appears beside the claim, separate from the page-build time, and a build check fails if any surface drifts past this boundary again.

title: The 184 gateway-gap works now resolve; our own gateway serves everything it holds
body: Second full census, run on the production monitor this time: 35,008 works, 106,392 files — the same set as 8/3. The 184 works whose media failed on a public gateway on 8/3 were three HLS playlists whose stream files were never on IPFS; each is now a plain MP4 on IPFS, and every affected token's on-chain reference (50 on Ethereum, 142 on Tezos) points at it. Separately, ipfs.feralfile.com had failed 4,448 probes on 8/3 — 44 thumbnail files that were never pinned on it; they are pinned now and it failed 0 probes today. Works with all media content-addressed and resolving on ipfs.io: 17,563 → 17,755. Twelve works had a single gateway probe fail at census time (ipfs.io: two HTTP 410 and one timeout; dweb.link: nine connection failures on its subdomain redirect). Each was re-probed once on 2026-08-26 with the same scanner: nine passed on every gateway and their rows were replaced, so the gateway-gap bucket is 0; three still failed on dweb.link only (they resolve on ipfs.io and on our gateway) and keep their original rows. The replaced rows are listed in the commit that made the change. 21 of the works are held by a Feral File contract and were skipped by the monitor's own walk; they were probed on 2026-08-26 with the same scanner and every file resolved on all three gateways, and their rows are in the same data file.

title: Look up a whole wallet, and take its pin list with you
body: Paste an Ethereum (0x…) or Tezos (tz…) address into the lookup and it returns every published work that address holds, plus a downloadable list of the unique content addresses behind them — one per line, ready for ipfs pin add. Holdings are read from the public indexers (Blockscout, TzKT) by the browser itself, so the page stays serverless and never sees the address. Works with no published content address yet are reported rather than dropped, and Bitmark-era works keep the token-ID path. Requested by collectors on launch day (feral-file/status#1).

title: The Bitmark-era repointing lands: works dependent on our CDN 17,247 → 11,389
body: Third full census (35,008 works, 106,392 files), the first since the 5,880 migrated Bitmark-era tokens were repointed on-chain to ipfs://. Works with all media content-addressed and resolving on ipfs.io: 17,755 → 23,619; works whose media depend on our CDN: 17,247 → 11,389 — the remainder is the phase-2 population (ops/cdn-retirement-phase2.md), all Ethereum, led by crystalline work (9,048). The raw run recorded 748 ipfs.io and 890 dweb.link failures: 747 and 721 of them HTTP 429 — the repointing moved ~11,000 files onto the IPFS probe path in one run and the public gateways rate-limited it (429 is deliberately never retried in-run); the rest were 167 dweb.link 504s, two 301s, and one ipfs.io 410 that served 200 on re-probe. Every one of the 699 affected tokens was re-probed with the census's own scanner, paced 2–5 s apart (tools/census-rescan, resumable variant): all 699 passed on every gateway and their rows were replaced, so the gateway-gap bucket is 0. The 21 works held by a Feral File contract were again missing from the monitor's own walk — its recover-by-refetch counter recorded 0, a bug to chase in the monitor — and were probed and appended exactly as on 8/25; every file resolved on all three gateways. Two real changes since 8/25, both server-side: the 878 imagedelivery.net thumbnail files now serve from our IPFS gateway, and the six works previously counted third-party-only now have a content-addressed image as well (their animations still run on aesthetic.computer), so no work is classified third-party-only this census.

title: Bitmark-era works reclassified: not yet migrated, no longer counted as depending on us
body: The depends-on-us tile bundled two different situations: 11,389 Ethereum/Tezos works whose media we must repoint (the CDN-retirement phase-2 population), and 4,959 Bitmark-era works never swapped to a collector chain. The second set now has its own class — not yet migrated — because both preconditions of independence are already in place: every series has a byte-verified archival copy on IPFS (2026-08-04), and a swap writes content-addressed references into the migrated token (it fails closed without them; the 5,880 tokens swapped before that guard existed were repointed on-chain 2026-09-01). Their published references still resolve only through our CDN until each collector migrates — the page and the per-work lookup say exactly that. status.json changed shape: bitmark_era moved out of depend_entirely_on_feralfile into a top-level not_yet_migrated_bitmark_era class.
